Rashi on Pesachim 24a:11:1.english: Neither have I removed - An explicit prohibition is derived for us concerning it in Yevamot, in [the chapter entitled] Ha'arel (Yevamot 73b).

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:12:1.hebrew: אין מזהירין - מדין קל וחומר. אף על פי שאדם דן קל וחומר מעצמו, אינה אזהרה ללאו; במסכת מכות (דף ה:) נפקא לן:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:12:1.english: We do not warn - From an a fortiori inference [kal vachomer]. Although a person may deduce an a fortiori inference on his own, it is not [valid as] a warning for a negative commandment; in Tractate Makkot (daf 5b) this is derived for us.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:12:2.hebrew: היקשא הוא - ולאו קל וחומר, דאיתקש "נדריך ונדבותיך" — דהיינו שלמים — למעשר דגן, דכתיב ביה: "לא בערתי ממנו בטמא", ותייתי לן מינה דאף קדשים לא יאכלו בטומאה. ו"לא בערתי ממנו בטמא", אע"ג דוידוי בעלמא הוא ואינו לאו — הא נפקא לן ביה איסור לאו ביבמות בהערל מהאי קרא ד"לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך". ולהלן הוא אומר בפסולי המוקדשים שנפדו (דברים ט״ו:כ״ב): "בשעריך תאכלנו הטמא והטהור יחדיו" — טמא וטהור אוכלין בקערה אחת, יש כאן טומאת בשר לטהור וטומאת הגוף לטמא; וקא אמר רחמנא גבי מעשר וקדשים: ההוא "בשעריך" דשראי לך ביה טומאה התם בפסולי המוקדשין — הכא "לא תאכל":
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:12:2.english: It is a juxtaposition - And not an a fortiori inference, for "your vows and your voluntary offerings" — which are peace-offerings — are juxtaposed to the tithe of grain, regarding which it is written: "I have not eaten of it in ritual impurity," and let it be derived for us from it that sacrificial food as well may not be eaten in ritual impurity. And [as for] "I have not eaten of it in ritual impurity," even though it is merely a confession and not a negative prohibition, behold, a negative prohibition regarding it is derived for us in Yevamot, in [the chapter entitled] Ha’arel, from this verse: "You may not eat within your gates [the tithe of your grain...]" (Deuteronomy 12:17). And elsewhere it says regarding disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed (Deuteronomy 15:22): "Within your gates you shall eat it, the impure and the pure alike" — an impure person and a pure person may eat from one dish; [thus] there is here ritual impurity of the meat for a pure person and ritual impurity of the body for an impure person. And the Merciful One states regarding tithes and sacrificial foods: That [manner of eating] "within your gates" in which I permitted ritual impurity to you there, with disqualified consecrated animals — here, "you may not eat" [in that manner].

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:15:1.english: [If one] ate a putita - A water-creeping creature.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:15:2.hebrew: לוקה ארבע - חד לאו בשרץ המים בתורת כהנים, דהוא ספר ויקרא, וחד במשנה תורה. ושני לאוין כתובים בתורת כהנים בשקצים סתם: ״לא תשקצו את נפשותיכם בכל השרץ השורץ ולא תטמאו בהן״, והכא לא כתיב ״על הארץ״, ומשמע: בין שרץ המים ובין שרץ הארץ — הרי ארבע:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:15:2.english: He is flogged with four [sets of lashes] - One negative commandment [is stated] regarding swarming creatures of the water in Torat Kohanim, which is the book of Leviticus, and one in Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy]. And two negative commandments are written in Torat Kohanim regarding detestable creatures in general: “You shall not make yourselves detestable with any swarming creature that swarms, neither shall you make yourselves defiled with them”; and here it is not written “upon the earth,” which implies both swarming creatures of the water and swarming creatures of the earth — behold, [there are] four.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:16:1.english: An ant - For it is a creeping creature of the earth.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:16:2.hebrew: לוקה חמש - הני תרי דסתם שרצים, וחד: ״וכל השרץ השורץ על הארץ שקץ הוא לא יאכל״, וחד: ״לכל השרץ השורץ על הארץ לא תאכלום כי שקץ הם״, וחד: ״ולא תטמאו את נפשותיכם בכל השרץ הרומש על הארץ״:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:16:2.english: [He] is flogged [with] five - Those two [prohibitions] of creeping things in general; and one: “And every creeping thing that swarms upon the earth is a detestable thing; it shall not be eaten”; and one: “Of all creeping things that swarm upon the earth, you shall not eat them, for they are a detestable thing”; and one: “And you shall not make yourselves impure with any creeping thing that moves upon the earth.”

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:1:1.hebrew: ואם אינו ענין - לאוסרם באכילה, דהא איסור אכילה בגופייהו כתיב. זו מדה בתורה: דבר שלא הוצרך לגופו, תנהו ענין לענין אחר ותלמוד דבר לדבר אחר. וכל המדות הלכה למשה מסיני:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:1:1.english: And if it does not apply to the matter [of] - To prohibit them from being eaten, for the prohibition of eating is written concerning themselves. This is a hermeneutical principle in the Torah: A matter that was not needed for its own [context], apply it to another matter, and derive one thing from another. And all the [hermeneutical] principles are a Halakhah to Moses from Sinai.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:3:1.hebrew: לימד על חטאת - פסולה, ששריפתה בקדש — בעזרה; דמ״והנה שורף״ לא הוה שמעינן מקום שריפתה היכן:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:3:1.english: Taught regarding a sin-offering - [That is,] a disqualified [sin-offering], that its burning [takes place] in the sacred place — in the [Temple] courtyard; for from “and behold, it was burned,” we would not have learned where its place of burning is.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:3:2.hebrew: פסולי - כל שאר קדשי קדשים, כגון: מנחה, ועולה, ואשם שנטמאו, או שנשפך דמן, ומנחה שלא נקטר קומצה, ואימורי קדשים קלים שנטמאו. ודוקא נקט הני, שמחיצתן בתוך חומת העזרה; אבל פסולי בשר קדשים קלים, שאכילתן בכל העיר — אף שריפתן, אם נפסלו, חוץ לעזרה הן. והכי נמי תנן באלו עוברין (לקמן פסחים מט.): ״שורפין לפני הבירה״, והיינו חוץ לעזרה, ושם היה בית הדשן לכך. וכן מפורש בזבחים בפר' טבול יום (זבחים ד' קד:):
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:3:2.english: Disqualified [offerings] - All other offerings of the most sacred order — such as a meal-offering, a burnt-offering, or a guilt-offering that became ritually impure or whose blood was spilled, and a meal-offering whose fistful was not burned [on the altar] — and sacrificial portions of offerings of minor sanctity that became ritually impure. And [the baraita] specifically mentioned these, whose boundary is within the wall of the Temple courtyard. But disqualified meat of offerings of minor sanctity, whose consumption is [permitted] throughout the entire city — even their burning, if they became disqualified, is outside the Temple courtyard. And so too we learned in [the chapter entitled] Ellu Overin (below, Pesachim 49a): “They are burned before the Birah” — and this is outside the Temple courtyard, and there was a place of ashes there for this [purpose]; and so it is explained in Zevachim in the chapter [entitled] Tevul Yom (Zevachim 104b).

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:4:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - ההוא מרבנן לר' שמואל בר נחמני, דאקשי ליה האי קושיא: ר' יונתן רבך נמי לא הוה מייתי איסור הנאה לכל איסורין מבקדש באש תשרף, דמבעי ליה לכדאמרת — שתשרף בעזרה, אלא מהאי קרא אמר להו:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:4:1.english: He said to him - That [one] of the Rabbis [said] to Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani, who had raised this objection to him: "Rabbi Yonatan, your teacher, also did not derive the prohibition of benefit for all [other] prohibitions from 'In the sacred place it shall be burned with fire,' as it is needed for that which you said — that it must be burned in the [Temple] courtyard; rather, from this verse he stated it to them:"

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:5:1.english: For behold, it is written: “And you shall burn” - This shows that it is not [something] to be eaten.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:5:2.hebrew: לכל איסורין - דוגמתן, שנאמר בהן לאו באכילתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:5:2.english: To all prohibitions - [Those] similar to them, regarding which a negative commandment is stated concerning their eating:

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:6:1.hebrew: מיבעי ליה לכדר' אלעזר - ליתן לא תעשה, דאי מושרפת, לא הוה ידעינן ביה איסור לאו למלקות:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:6:1.english: It is needed for [the teaching] of Rabbi Elazar - To establish a negative commandment; for if [it were derived only] from “and you shall burn,” we would not know from it a negative prohibition for lashes.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:6:2.hebrew: כל שבקודש פסול - מדכתיב כי קודש הוא יתירה, לרבות על שאר פסולי קדשי קדשים בלאו, כגון פיגול, ויוצא, ונשפך דמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:6:2.english: Whatever has been disqualified in the sacred [place] - Since “because it is sacred” is written superfluously, [it comes] to include other disqualified most holy sacrifices under a negative prohibition, such as piggul [an offering disqualified by improper intent], and yotzei [meat taken outside the courtyard], and [an offering whose] blood was spilled.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:1.hebrew: מקרא קמא - "וכל חטאת". ולאו מ"באש תשרף", דאיצטריך לומר שישרף בעזרה, אלא מ"לא תאכל". ליכתוב "באש תשרף" — אלמא לאו בר אכילה הוא, וממילא נפקא לן ביה נמי איסור לאו מהא דרבי אלעזר, דמפיק מ"לא יאכל כי קודש הוא" כל פסולי קדשים:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:1.english: The first verse - [Namely,] “And any sin-offering” (Leviticus 6:23). And [the derivation is] not from “it shall be burnt with fire,” as that is needed to say that it must be burnt in the [Temple] courtyard, but rather from “it shall not be eaten.” Let [the verse] write: “It shall be burnt with fire” — [from which it is] evident that it is not fit for eating, and a negative prohibition would also automatically be derived for us regarding it from that [teaching] of Rabbi Elazar, who derives from “it shall not be eaten, for it is holy” (Exodus 29:34) [a prohibition for] all disqualified consecrated items.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:2.hebrew: לכל איסורין - דוגמתן, שנאמר בהן לאו באכילתן:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:2.english: To all prohibitions - [Those] similar to them, regarding which a negative commandment was stated concerning their eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:3.hebrew: ואם אינו ענין לאכילה - דהא בגופייהו כתיב, תנהו ענין להנאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:7:3.english: And if it does not apply to eating - For [a prohibition against eating] is already written regarding [those prohibitions] themselves, [so] apply it to the matter of [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:8:1.english: The verse said: "And the leftover" - For it should have written: "And you shall burn it with fire."

Rashi on Pesachim 24a:9:1.hebrew: לאו שבכללות - כגון זה, שנכלל כל הפסולין יחד:
Rashi on Pesachim 24a:9:1.english: A negative commandment stated in general terms - Such as this, where all disqualified [offerings] are included together.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:11:1.hebrew: אם אינו ענין לגופו דאתי בקל וחומר ממעשר - ואם תאמר: והא איצטריך לרביעי בקודש, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא (דף יט.)? וי"ל: דלא ליכתוב "לא יאכל", אלא "ישרף":
Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:11:1.english: “If it does not refer to the matter itself, as it is derived by an a fortiori inference from tithe” - And if you say: But wasn't [this phrase] needed for [deriving the status of] a fourth [degree of impurity] in consecrated items, as we say in the first chapter (19a)? And one can say: Let [the verse] not write “it shall not be eaten,” but rather [only] “it shall be burned.”

Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:12:1.hebrew: הקישא הוא - תימה: אמאי קרי ליה הקישא? תיפוק ליה דקודש כתיב בהדיא בקרא: "ובכורות בקרך וצאנך", ואזהרה למעשר נמי יליף מהאי קרא! וי"ל: דצריך הקישא משום איסור הנאה — דלא תוקי קרא דוהבשר לאיסור הנאה, שיהא בלאו; דבפ' שני דשבת (דף כה.) לא ילפי' איסור הנאה בשמן קדש שנטמא אלא ממעשר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:12:1.english: "It is a juxtaposition" - It is astonishing: Why does [the Gemara] call it a juxtaposition? Let [the prohibition] be derived from [the fact] that consecrated [offerings] are written explicitly in the verse: "And the firstborn of your herd and your flock" [Deuteronomy 12:17], and the warning for [impure] tithe is also derived from this [same] verse! And it may be said that a juxtaposition is necessary because of the prohibition of deriving benefit — so that you should not establish the verse of "And the meat" [Leviticus 7:19] for the prohibition of benefit, such that it would be [prohibited] by a negative commandment; for in the second chapter of Shabbat (25a), we derive the prohibition of benefit with regard to consecrated oil that became impure only from [the second] tithe.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:12:2.hebrew: דכתיב לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך - האי לא חשיב לאו שבכללות, מדלא כתיב "מעשר דגנך ובכורות בקרך לא תוכל לאכלם"; ש"מ ליחודי לאו אכל חד דכתי' בקרא אתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:12:2.english: As it is written: “You may not eat within your gates” - This is not considered a generalized negative commandment, since it is not written: “The tithe of your grain and the firstborn of your herd, you may not eat them”; learn from this that it comes to designate a [distinct] negative commandment for each [item] that is written in the verse.

Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:1:1.hebrew: ואם אינו ענין לאכילה - לא אתי שפיר, דהיכי מצי לאוקמי' באיסור אכילה, דהא כתיב: "באש תשרף":
Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:1:1.english: "And if it does not apply to the matter of eating" - This does not work out well, for how could [the Gemara] apply it to the prohibition of eating, when it is written: "It shall be burnt with fire"?

Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:9:1.hebrew: הא אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות - הקשה הר"ר אליעזר ממיץ, דבאלו הן הלוקין (מכות יג.) אמר דלאו דנותר ופיגול הוה בכלל הלוקין. ואמאי? והא לאו שבכללות הוא! ותירץ, דלגבי נותר שמפורש בהדיא, דכתיב: "ושרפת את הנותר באש לא יאכל כי קדש הוא" — לא חשיב לאו שבכללות, ופיגול נמי גמרינן "עון" "עון" מנותר. אך קשה, דבפרק בתרא דמכות (דף יז: יח.), גבי זר שאכל עולה לפני זריקה לוקה חמש, פריך: ולילקי נמי מדרבי אלעזר, דאמר: כל שבקודש פסול! ומאי קושיא? והא לאו שבכללות הוא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 24a:9:1.english: "Behold, one is not flogged for a negative commandment stated in general terms" - Rabbi Eliezer of Metz raised a difficulty: For in [the chapter entitled] Elu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 13a), [the Gemara] states that the negative prohibition of notar [remnant] and piggul [an offering invalidated by improper intention] was included among [the prohibitions for which] one is flogged. But why? Isn't it a negative commandment stated in general terms? And he answered: Regarding notar, which is explicitly specified — as it is written: "And you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, because it is holy" (Exodus 29:34) — it is not considered a negative commandment stated in general terms; and regarding piggul as well, we derive [it via the verbal analogy of] "iniquity" [and] "iniquity" from notar. However, this is difficult, for in the final chapter of Makkot (17b–18a), regarding a non-priest who ate [meat of] a burnt-offering before the sprinkling [of its blood and] is flogged five [times, the Gemara] objects: And let him also be flogged based on [the teaching of] Rabbi Elazar, who said: Anything in the Sanctuary that has become disqualified [is subject to a negative commandment against eating it]! But what is the question? Isn't it a negative commandment stated in general terms?
